title: Magnus Carlsen Vs Wesley So | FTX Crypto Finals Commentary

moves.spoken: Black meets the king-pawn with c5 — the Sicilian, the great fighting reply when Black wants an unbalanced game rather than a symmetrical one.
teaches: The Sicilian unbalances the game from move one

moves.spoken: White develops the knight to f3, the natural Open Sicilian move-order — but he has a quieter idea in mind than d4.
There it is — the bishop checks from b5, the Moscow Variation. White sidesteps the sharp theory of the Open Sicilian and steers for a calmer, positional game.
teaches: Bb5+ is the Moscow — a positional anti-Sicilian

moves.spoken: Black has three ways to block the check, and the choice is a statement of intent. Dropping the bishop to d7 offers a trade and the peaceful road; the knight to d7, the combative one — it keeps the pieces on and plays for a win. Black takes the fighting square.
teaches: How you meet Bb5+ chooses between a peaceful and a fighting game

moves.spoken: White simply castles, tucking the king away and keeping the tension. The engine calls the position dead level — a classic, slow Moscow middlegame is brewing.
Black develops the knight to f6, hitting the centre and completing the kingside pieces.
The rook lifts to e1, backing the e-pawn and readying the centre. Nothing forcing — both sides are just improving, and the balance holds.
Black nudges the pawn to a6, putting the question to the bishop and gaining a little queenside space in the bargain.
teaches: ...a6 questions the bishop and claims queenside space

moves.spoken: Rather than trade on d7 or sidle to a4, the bishop retreats all the way to f1. It keeps the bishop pair and stays flexible — and here the engine even gives Black the whisper of an edge, exactly the sort of slow pull Black was fighting for.
teaches: Retreat to keep a flexible bishop rather than trade it off

moves.spoken: On the recap: this is the Moscow, and the fork in the road was that check on b5. The bishop back to d7 is the peaceful choice — a quick trade and a quiet game; the knight to d7 keeps everything on the board and plays for the full point.

Take the peaceful line with the bishop to d7. From here White can push d4 and transpose into an Open-Sicilian hedgehog, a cramped-but-springy structure; or clamp the centre with c4, the Maroczy bind, trading winning chances for a lasting space grip. The choice sets the whole character of the game.
teaches: d4 gives a hedgehog; c4 is the space-gaining Maroczy bind
